mechanisms.name: `Certificate.spec.privateKey.rotationPolicy` default changes from `Never` to `Always` (BREAKING)
resourcesConsumers: consumers outside the repo (WAF, firewall, allow-list pinning leaf key or fingerprint) - unknown
mechanisms.mechanism: The default changes so that each renewal generates a new private key. The `DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways` feature gate defaults to on (beta) and the chart values here do not touch it. ledger-tls and checkout-tls do not set rotationPolicy, so their behaviour changes: each renewal generates a new key where before the key was reused. The first rotation should happen at the next scheduled renewal, 480h (20 days) after each cert's last issuance. An accidental key rotation of the root CA at renewal would be the dangerous outcome, because its public key is the trust anchor for every ca.crt in the mesh. New, tiny race: because key and cert now change together, a read straddling the kubelet symlink swap could pair the old cert with the new key. For checkout's curl this means one failed call, retried 30s later. For nginx it only matters if a reload lands in that instant. The assessment calls this 'negligible but real'. External consumers that pin the leaf key or fingerprint would break on rotation.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The assessment's own label is 'applies, benign on the evidence'. The verdict says the change 'does change behaviour for two certificates here' but 'From the evidence in the repo, that change is benign' and 'neutralised where it matters most (the mesh root CA)'. mesh-root-ca is protected because the prod overlay sets `rotationPolicy: Never` explicitly, and the pki Argo app points at that overlay. Caveats: the base mesh-root-ca.yaml has no rotationPolicy, so only the overlay protects it, and the value appears redacted (the assessment relied on a comment saying it is the digest of 'Never' and did not verify this independently). No immediate re-issuance is expected at upgrade time, but this is 'an inference from the docs and not something I observed, so test it'. Nothing in the repo pins the leaf public key: ledger verifies clients only against the CA, and checkout verifies ledger only with --cacert. Secret updates are consistent: tls.crt, tls.key and ca.crt are written to one Secret, mounted as a directory volume with no subPath or envFrom. Separately, there is a pre-existing risk that key rotation does not create: ledger's nginx loads the cert once and nothing reloads it, so an unrestarted pod will serve an expired cert after 720h with or without the upgrade.
citedEvidence: rendered CRD diff: field text changes to "Default is `Always`"
`DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways` feature gate defaults to on (beta); chart values do not touch it
prod overlay sets `privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never` on mesh-root-ca
redacted value with comment saying it is the digest of "Never"
Deployments mount the Secret as a directory volume, no `subPath`, no `envFrom`
no reloader, sidecar or `nginx -s reload` in the repo
assumptions: No re-issuance at upgrade time: the renewal triggers are expiry, renewBefore, spec mismatch or manual renew, and a rotationPolicy change is not one of them (an inference from the docs, not observed)
The redacted mesh-root-ca rotationPolicy value is 'Never', relying on the file comment (not independently verified)
There are no external consumers pinning the leaf key (none visible)
missingEvidence: Live value of mesh-root-ca rotationPolicy (seen only as a redacted value)
Whether re-issuance occurs at upgrade time (not observed)
External consumers that pin the leaf key or fingerprint
How the ledger nginx cert reload or expiry is handled today
Live status.notAfter and renewalTime for the certificates
recommendedValidation: kubectl get certificate -A -o wide plus status.notAfter and renewalTime for mesh-root-ca, ledger-tls and checkout-tls, to see when the first rotation will fire
kubectl get certificate mesh-root-ca -n cert-manager -o jsonpath='{.spec.privateKey.rotationPolicy}' and confirm it is literally Never live and in the raw Git file
Check for external consumers that pin the ledger or checkout leaf public key or fingerprint
Staging: upgrade and confirm no Certificate is re-issued at upgrade time by comparing status.revision
Staging: cmctl renew ledger-tls checkout-tls; confirm the leaf key changes, the root CA key and ca.crt are unchanged, and checkout still reaches ledger over mTLS (watch for 'ledger call failed')
Staging: force a mesh-root-ca renewal; confirm its key is unchanged and the leaf chain validates against old and new ca.crt

Optional edits: set rotationPolicy explicitly on ledger-tls and checkout-tls (the gate goes GA in 1.19 and cannot be turned off); move rotationPolicy: Never into platform/pki/base/mesh-root-ca.yaml; decide on a reloader or restart for ledger

mechanisms.name: `Certificate.spec.revisionHistoryLimit` default changes from nil to 1 (potentially breaking)
resourcesConsumers: CertificateRequests for mesh-root-ca, ledger-tls and checkout-tls
anything outside the repo that uses old CertificateRequests (audit tooling, log shipping, runbooks)
mechanisms.mechanism: On upgrade, the controller garbage-collects stale CertificateRequests and keeps the latest revision for each Certificate. The only loss is history, for anyone who uses it for audit or forensics.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The assessment's own label is 'applies, low impact'. Nothing in the repo reads CertificateRequests (no RBAC, scripts, alerts or other consumers). CertificateRequests are controller-created and not tracked in Git. If history is wanted, set revisionHistoryLimit explicitly.
citedEvidence: rendered CRD diff shows "Default value is `1`"
missingEvidence: Whether anything outside the repo (audit tooling, log shipping, runbooks) depends on old CertificateRequests
recommendedValidation: Check for anything outside the repo that reads CertificateRequests
Staging: count CertificateRequests before and after the upgrade to confirm the GC behaviour and that nothing breaks
Set revisionHistoryLimit explicitly if CertificateRequest history is needed

mechanisms.name: ACME HTTP-01 Ingress `pathType: Exact` (BREAKING for ingress-nginx and OpenShift)
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: There are no ACME issuers, Ingresses or Gateways; the environment uses only selfSigned and CA issuers. The assessment verified this by reading every manifest in env/. The `ACMEHTTP01IngressPathTypeExact` gate exists only in v1.18.1 and later and is irrelevant.
missingEvidence: Whether the live cluster has Issuers, ClusterIssuers, Certificates or Ingresses not in the repo (ORIENTATION.md says none, not verified)
recommendedValidation: Confirm the live cluster has no Issuers, ClusterIssuers, Certificates or Ingresses that are not in this repo

mechanisms.name: Chart and rendered changes
resourcesConsumers: controller, webhook, cainjector, startupapicheck images and acmesolver flag
cert-manager-controller-challenges ClusterRole and binding, replaced by cert-manager-dns01-controller-challenges and cert-manager-http01-controller-challenges
CRDs (signatureAlgorithm, ACME profile, Vault serverName, ciss/iss short names)
mechanisms.mechanism: Version labels and images change to v1.18.0. Controller args are otherwise unchanged. Webhook probes change from numeric port 6080 to the named port `healthcheck`. The challenges ClusterRole and binding are split into dns01 and http01 variants and the old pair is removed; Argo prune deletes the old pair and creates four new ones. The orders role moves a few rules. CRDs gain additive fields and the ciss/iss short names, with a theoretical short-name collision. AdditionalCertificateOutputFormats doc text is dropped because the feature is GA. Metrics and ServiceMonitor port names change.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The named port resolves (`containerPort: 6080, name: healthcheck` in rendered/to.yaml). The RBAC permissions are ACME-only and the cluster has no ACME; none of this touches the CA issuer or Certificate paths. If the AppProject `platform` restricts cluster-scoped kinds (not in the repo, could not check), confirm ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding are allowed; 'They are already in use, so this should be fine.' No manifests set the new CRD fields. `crds.keep: true` is retained. AdditionalCertificateOutputFormats is unused. Metrics changes are irrelevant because prometheus.enabled is false.
citedEvidence: chart values.yaml files not diffed line by line (Bash denied); chart-level effects judged from the rendered diff
assumptions: The AppProject `platform` allows ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding since they are already in use ('this should be fine')

Confirm the Argo AppProject `platform` and its resource whitelists allow the new ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding names

mechanisms.name: Security advisory GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258
mechanisms.mechanism: Challenge resources can bypass the DNS01 solver policy. Affected versions are >= 1.18.0 and <= 1.20.2; patched versions are 1.19.6 and 1.20.3. Exploitation needs a ClusterIssuer with a DNS01 solver and permission to create ACME Challenges. There is no patched 1.18.x, so staying on the 1.18 line leaves it unfixed.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: This environment has no ACME issuer, so it is not exploitable here. The advisory does not list v1.17.2, but the assessment does not know whether 1.17 was tested, so 1.17.2 should not be read as unaffected.
citedEvidence: GHSA advisory page: "Affected versions >= 1.18.0, <= 1.20.2", patched 1.19.6 and 1.20.3
missingEvidence: Whether 1.17 was tested against the advisory
recommendedValidation: Decide whether to go straight to 1.19.6 or 1.20.3 for the advisory fix (outside this question)

mechanisms.name: Version choice: target v1.18.6, not v1.18.0 (later 1.18 patch releases)
mechanisms.mechanism: v1.18.5 fixes a moderate DoS (GHSA-gx3x-vq4p-mhhv, a DNS-response panic) and an infinite re-issuance loop when an issuer returns a certificate whose public key does not match the CSR. v1.18.6 fixes CVE-2025-68121 (Go bump). v1.18.3 fixes an unwanted renewal when issuerRef kind or group is omitted.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The v1.18.3 issue is not a risk because kind and group are explicit in every Certificate here. The assessment recommends targeting v1.18.6.
recommendedValidation: If pinning 1.18.6, re-render to confirm the diff is still just the above
Decide whether to go straight to 1.19.6 or 1.20.3

mechanisms.name: Things that look fine but do not prove runtime compatibility
resourcesConsumers: webhook (single replica, validating and mutating webhooks fail closed)
mechanisms.mechanism: The Certificate manifests are unchanged, but their effective behaviour changes through the controller default. With a single webhook replica and fail-closed webhooks, creating or updating cert-manager resources is briefly blocked during rollout. If Argo does not handle the startupapicheck Job cleanly as a hook, the sync could look stuck. Argo does not wait on webhook readiness unless health checks cover it. Kubernetes 1.31 support by 1.18.0 was not confirmed.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Existing mTLS traffic is unaffected by the webhook rollout. CRDs update in wave 0 before the pki and payments apps in waves 1 and 2, which is good.
citedEvidence: Kubernetes compatibility page not in the supplied upstream material
missingEvidence: Confirmation that the cluster runs Kubernetes 1.31
recommendedValidation: Confirm the cluster runs Kubernetes 1.31 as stated and that 1.18 supports it
Staging: observe the webhook rollout with 1 replica and confirm the Argo sync completes cleanly

overall.recommendation: Proceed with conditions: proceed subject to the read-only live-cluster checks and staging tests in 'Missing information / tests' and a few optional hardening edits. Target v1.18.6 rather than v1.18.0. Take a backup of the mesh-root-ca, ledger-tls and checkout-tls Secrets and have a rollback path (re-pin targetRevision: v1.17.2). The assessment states that nothing about the live cluster could be checked.
overall.quote: I would proceed, subject to the checks in "Missing information / tests" and a few hardening edits.
